chalisa.do1: I call to mind Girijā's dear son, all blessing and the bringer of blessing, with the great face of a mighty elephant,
who removes obstacles and destroys enemies and disease.
chalisa.cau1: Victory to Gaṇeśa, renowned for strength and wisdom; Vakratuṇḍa, of the curved trunk, you are an ocean of learning.
chalisa.cau2: Son of Śiva, worshipped by the whole world, your body thrills with delight and you are always joyful.
chalisa.cau3: Your form is calm and your face is vermilion; you drive away evil thinking and take away distress.
chalisa.cau4: The moon is enthroned on your diadem and crown; a trident and a book shine in your hands.
chalisa.cau5: O beloved lord of Ṛddhi and Siddhi, you follow the word of your mother and father.
chalisa.cau6: He who loves to ride the mouse: to him I give myself.
chalisa.cau7: All people sing your name, and it destroys the sins of ten million births.
chalisa.cau8: Among all, your worship comes first; your beloved name is unmoving and undying.
chalisa.cau9: When people in sorrow worship you, you take away their troubles in a moment.
chalisa.cau10: O dear brother of the six-faced Kārttikeya, speech itself has grown weary singing your glory.
chalisa.cau11: Girijā brought you forth; she fashioned your body from the grime of her own.
chalisa.cau12: She gave you the fine office of doorkeeper and seated you at the entrance.
chalisa.cau13: Then your father Śiva came, his austerities done; seeing you, he was much taken aback.
chalisa.cau14: He asked: Who are you, and where have you come from? Who has set you in this place?
chalisa.cau15: You said: I am Pārvatī's son; I am the doorkeeper of this entrance.
chalisa.cau16: He said: Umā has had no child, no son to sustain the family.
chalisa.cau17: Then how are you her child? That is the doubt in my mind.
chalisa.cau18: Hearing your father's words, you, the child, said: I am the sustainer of the family.
chalisa.cau19: Do not doubt this in the least; give ear to my words.
chalisa.cau20: Mother is bathing inside, having set her son as doorkeeper.
chalisa.cau21: She will come in a moment, at this very time, and appearing, she will clear away the doubt to good effect.
chalisa.cau22: Then, hearing such words, Śiva conceived a new thought in his heart.
chalisa.cau23: He stepped forward to go inside; then you came forward in front of him.
chalisa.cau24: You said: Father, do not take a step; please do not press a quarrel with a child.
chalisa.cau25: Enraged, Śiva raised his trident, cut through your neck, and stepped forward.
chalisa.cau26: Śiva went to Girijā and said: Where is a wife's faithfulness?
chalisa.cau27: How did you bear this son? You have disgraced the name of a faithful wife's truth.
chalisa.cau28: Then Umā told all about your birth; she hid nothing and kept nothing back from Śiva.
chalisa.cau29: Hearing Girijā's whole story, Śiva, who knows the truth of māyā (the power of illusion), laughed.
chalisa.cau30: At once he sent messengers of auspicious face; they cut off an elephant's head and brought it.
chalisa.cau31: Śiva set it on the body, breathed life into it and gave you a name:
chalisa.cau32: Gaṇapati, Gaṇapati, son of Girijā, the first to be worshipped, who burns away the disease of the fear of worldly existence.
chalisa.cau33: From that very day the world has worshipped you; mighty of body, you are content and full of joy.
chalisa.cau34: The two of you made the circuit of the earth; there the six-faced Kārttikeya made his plan.
chalisa.cau35: Mounted on his peacock, he went on ahead and ahead; O Vakratuṇḍa, he raced off alongside you.
chalisa.cau36: Then Nārada counselled you, and not the least trace of doubt was left.
chalisa.cau37: You went around your mother and father, and, having so circled the earth, won glory.
chalisa.cau38: Blessed, blessed are you, rider of the mouse! Lord, the whole world gives itself to you.
chalisa.cau39: May your grace rest always on Ḍāsnā; Lord, this is my great wish.
chalisa.cau40: Whoever reads this Chālīsā with faith, you are their companion, O Gaurīśa.
chalisa.do2: Son of Śiva, remover of distress, holy, spotless and peerless,
dwell ever in my heart together with Śiva and Girijā, O king of happiness.
